experiment: AgentX 15 min at c1/c4/c16 for vLLM, SGLang (official MI355X recipes, MI350P memory fixes) and unmodified UnieInfra.
result: c16: vLLM 505.9 out tok/s, SGLang 376.5. UnieInfra c1 78.3 tok/s; its c4 run crashed (all ranks SIGSEGV in rocr AsyncEventsLoop).
decision: Investigate the UnieInfra crash before any optimization.

experiment: Root disk filled during crashes.
result: Each crashed rank wrote a multi-GB apport core dump (58 GB RSS + Engram tables).
decision: Disable core dumps in all three server launchers (ulimit core=0). Mount the spare SATA disk at /data.

experiment: Long-prefill repro: 3 concurrent ~254K-token prompts x3 rounds; then single prompts of 330K, 381K, 425K, 433K tokens.
result: Concurrent 254K prompts pass. A single prompt crashes once its position crosses (381,257, 393,216]; 381K passes.
decision: Crash depends on one sequence's depth, not concurrency.

experiment: 433K prompt with --max-total-tokens 4M, --disable-prefill-graph, --gpu-memory-utilization 0.8.
result: Crashes in all three.
decision: Not KV budget, prefill graphs or memory pressure.

experiment: 433K prompt with HIP_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1, and separately with --disable-overlap-schedule.
result: Both pass (overlap off: 434K prefill in 75.8 s). Kernel log shows no GPU page fault, only a CPU segfault.
decision: Host-side ROCm runtime race under the overlap schedule; run benchmarks with overlap off until fixed.

experiment: AgentX c1/c4/c16 for UnieInfra with --disable-overlap-schedule.
result: 73.4 / 135.5 / 335.8 out tok/s; c1 decode about 12% slower than with overlap.
decision: Workaround only; overlap must come back.

experiment: gfx950 CSA2 indexer ignored the 512 MiB logits option and used a hard-coded 32 MiB budget, so launches per prefill chunk grew with history (~23K at 393K).
result: 512 MiB budget: 434K prompt passes with overlap on, prefill 62 s (vs 76 s overlap off). Indexer tests pass.
decision: Keep. Crash fixed, overlap back on.

experiment: Indexer key loads: page_stride_bytes was do_not_specialize (byte loads); let it specialize, waves_per_eu 2 -> 8, share one key tile across both head groups.
result: 96 rows x 75K: 2332 -> 617 us (3.8x). 16 req at 150K context: 694 -> 1005 decode tok/s.
decision: Keep.

experiment: RCCL vs Iris all-reduce via --force-deterministic-rsag.
result: 16 req short context: 73 -> 79 tok/s/user (later shown to be noise once the indexer improved).
decision: Used for the c16 AgentX run below; revisited in #16.

experiment: AgentX c16 with #7, #8 and RCCL.
result: 508.1 out tok/s (+51% vs 335.8), RPM 28.5, TTFT p50 254 ms, tok/s/user 85.0. vLLM 505.9, SGLang 376.5.
decision: Matches vLLM throughput; per-user decode still about half of vLLM.

experiment: MXFP8 decode GEMM NUM_XCDS 8 -> 4 (MI350P has 4 XCDs).
result: Total over all DSv4.1 decode shapes: +0.4%.
decision: Rejected.

experiment: Share one key load across a request's 6 DSpark rows (row grouping).
result: 617 -> 3536 us (slower). Rows sharing keys vs all-distinct keys cost the same (617 vs 637 us): L2 already absorbs the reuse.
decision: Rejected.

experiment: Tile width sweep: 16/32/64/128 rows x 1/2/4/8 waves; score chunk 128-2048.
result: 16 rows, 1 wave best everywhere; chunk 1024 best for big work, 256 for small. 96 rows x 75K: 617 -> 331 us; 192 x 150K: 2341 -> 1173 us.
decision: Keep, with work-sized chunk buckets (256/512/1024). GSM8K 92.7% (threshold 90%).

experiment: Auto-route all AMD collectives to RCCL on PCIe-only hosts (KFD XGMI detection).
result: n=16 79 tok/s (same as Iris); n=1 155 tok/s vs 202 with Iris. Long context c16: RCCL 1026 vs Iris 1003 decode tok/s.
decision: Rejected and dropped: Iris is better at low batch and ties elsewhere.

experiment: Batch-1 decode profile with Iris.
result: GPU busy only 75%: about 4 ms per step waiting for the host; MoE 22%, MXFP8 GEMM 17%, Iris all-reduce 17%.
decision: Next target: host launch overhead at low batch.

experiment: ROCm env sweep: HIP_FORCE_DEV_KERNARG=1, +GPU_MAX_HW_QUEUES=2, +DEBUG_CLR_GRAPH_PACKET_CAPTURE=1.
result: n=1 tok/s/user: default 139-145, dev kernarg 191-196, +hwq2 197-199, +packet 148-181. Run-to-run noise large.
decision: Repeat A/B interleaved before adopting; paused to fill the benchmark matrix.

experiment: vLLM/SGLang c32-c128 round.
result: All 6 failed to start: vLLM cold model load from the SATA /data copy exceeded its engine startup timeout; SGLang's MI355X c32+ cells (tails 2048/4096, 64+ running) leave no KV room on 144 GB.
decision: vLLM/SGLang read the NVMe model copy again; SGLang c32+: tails 1024/512, 64 running. vLLM c32 rerun: 745.9 out tok/s.

experiment: Full matrix to remove gaps: SGLang c32/64/128, vLLM c64/128, current UnieInfra c1/c4/c16/c32/c64/c128.
result: SGLang c32/c64: 316.7/282.7 out tok/s (falls past c16: KV-bound queueing, TTFT p90 143 s/404 s). SGLang c128 hit the AiPerf timeout (40 min warmup). vLLM c64: 1028.1 out tok/s, 71.5 RPM.
decision: Per the user, compare against vLLM only: SGLang c128 not rerun; UnieInfra's six long cells deferred to the final build. AiPerf timeout raised to duration+5400 s.

experiment: Where UnieInfra's GPU time goes in AgentX c16 (from the server batch log).
result: 6.78M new prefill tokens in ~20 min (90% prefix-cache hits); prefill takes roughly half or more of GPU time, and only ~9 requests decode at once.
decision: Target for 2x vLLM: prefill speed and scaling to c32/c64, measured with 5-minute AgentX runs.

experiment: UnieInfra c64, 5-minute AgentX (commit 27314382), vs vLLM c64 (15 min).
result: 746.9 out tok/s, 62 RPM, TTFT p50 0.24 s, request latency 10.6 s. vLLM c64: 1028.1 out tok/s, 71.5 RPM, TTFT p50 22 s, request latency 30.1 s. vLLM c128 collapses to 355.0 out tok/s.
decision: UnieInfra serves each request 3x faster but RPM is similar: see #21.

experiment: AgentX pacing rules (aiperf inferencex_agentx_mvp scenario).
result: The scenario forbids ignoring trace delays: each lane replays the recorded user think time between turns (idle gaps capped at 300 s). From vLLM c64: 53.7 s per lane cycle = 30.1 s request + ~23.6 s think time.
decision: At equal concurrency, faster requests can give at most ~1.5x vLLM. 2x vLLM's best (1028 at c64) means sustaining c128 at ~30 s request latency, where vLLM collapses. Measure UnieInfra c128 next.

experiment: UnieInfra c128, 5-minute AgentX (stopped during warmup).
result: Saturated by prefill: one 16K-token chunk per step, 1 request running and 123 queued, no decode; 22.7K new prefill tokens/s.
decision: Prefill throughput is the bottleneck under load. Stopped the run to profile prefill.

experiment: Prefill profile: 4 steps of a 100K-token prompt (16K chunks).
result: RCCL all-reduce 47% of GPU time (2 x 168 MB per layer, ~4.6 ms each, ~55 GB/s bus bandwidth, the PCIe limit); indexer topk+select 15%; MXFP8 GEMM 6%; sparse prefill attention 5%; MoE 9%.
decision: Cut communication: try Iris at prefill sizes, then INT8 payloads.

experiment: Large all-reduce variants on 4x MI350P: RCCL, RCCL RS+AG, INT8 all-to-all+all-gather, Iris two-shot.
result: 168 MB: RCCL 6.19 ms, RS+AG 7.42, INT8 a2a+ag 8.10 (all-to-all is slow across sockets), Iris 5.51. 42 MB: RCCL 1.87, Iris 1.33.
decision: Use Iris for prefill sizes on PCIe hosts; INT8 needs a quantized Iris kernel, not RCCL primitives.

experiment: Lift Iris all-reduce caps to 256 MB on PCIe-only AMD hosts (KFD XGMI detection).
result: 104K-token prompt prefill 4.1-4.2 s -> 3.6-3.7 s (~10%). GSM8K 92.7%.
decision: Keep.

experiment: Iris pull two-shot with INT8 payloads (32-element groups, FP32 scales): quantize, reduce-scatter in FP32, requantize, gather. Swept tile rows, programs, warps, vector width.
result: Correct (relative error 7.7e-3 vs 1.7e-3 for BF16), but 168 MB takes 4.93 ms vs 5.11 ms for BF16 Iris (~27 GB/s effective vs ~49 GB/s), and ~0.3-1 ms fixed cost at small sizes.
decision: Shelved: needs BF16-two-shot-level load tuning to pay off, and adds two INT8 roundings. Kernel kept outside the tree.

experiment: Chunked prefill 32K instead of 16K (with Iris prefill all-reduce).
result: 104K-token prompt 4.2-4.3 s (16K chunks: 3.6-3.7 s). Three concurrent 104K prompts all finish at 12.2 s: prefill runs one chunk at a time, ~25.6K tok/s either way.
decision: Rejected; keep 16K.

experiment: Prefill profile after the Iris change (4 steps of a 100K-token prompt).
result: Iris two-shot all-reduce (with fused mHC post) 44%, indexer topk+select 16%, MoE 10%, MXFP8 GEMM 7%, sparse prefill attention 6.5%. Communication still runs at the PCIe limit.
decision: Remaining big lever is overlapping communication with compute (two micro-batches per prefill step), a multi-day change; measure current standing with the stress test first.

experiment: Stress test (AgentX corpus, think time removed via --ignore-trace-delays, unofficial), c32, 5 minutes, UnieInfra db3956be vs vLLM.
result: UnieInfra 88.7 RPM, 1111 out tok/s, 183K in tok/s, request latency 23.0 s. vLLM 45.5 RPM, 815 out tok/s, 110K in tok/s, 45.5 s. RPM 1.95x, input 1.67x, output 1.36x (output lengths differ: 751 vs 1076 in this window).
decision: Saturated server capacity is already ~1.7-2x vLLM by request and prefill rate; continue with communication overlap.

experiment: INT8 Iris all-reduce, second tuning round: group 32/64/128, 16-byte loads, 84-128 programs, 4-8 warps.
result: Best (group 128, 64-row tiles, 84 programs, 8 warps): 168 MB 4.55 ms vs 5.12 ms BF16 Iris (-11%), 42 MB 1.44 vs 1.33 ms; relative error 9.3e-3.
decision: Rejected: ~5% prefill at best, with two INT8 roundings. Communication overlap is the better lever.

experiment: Can an all-reduce overlap compute on MI350P? 84 MB all-reduce on a side stream next to BF16 GEMMs.
result: RCCL hides 64% of its 2.94 ms; Iris hides only 30% of its 2.61 ms (its spinning workgroups take CUs).
decision: Overlap designs must put RCCL on a side stream, not Iris.

experiment: Row-chunked prefill FFN overlap: attention and MoE all-reduces of 2 or 4 row chunks through RCCL on a side stream, overlapping the other chunks' mHC + MoE compute (eager prefill >= 4096 rows).
result: Needle-in-haystack 6/6 correct, but a 104K-token prefill takes 4.3-4.6 s (2 chunks) and 4.2-4.3 s (4 chunks) vs 3.6-3.7 s with serial Iris: RCCL is slower than Iris, the FFN window is too short to hide it, and chunked MoE is less efficient.
decision: Rejected and reverted. On this PCIe-only box, overlapping with RCCL loses to serial Iris; full two-batch overlap would net ~20% at best for multi-day work.

experiment: Official AgentX c128, 15 min, UnieInfra db3956be.
result: 2.9 RPM, 4.8 out tok/s, ITL p50 4.8 s, 45 requests. Server log: prefill-only rounds (#running-req 1, #queue-req 50-252, #cached-token 0).
decision: UnieInfra collapses at c128; investigate scheduler admission.

experiment: Stress sweep (think time removed, 5 min/point), official recipe parameters: UnieInfra db3956be vs vLLM, c1/c16/c32/c64/c128.
result: RPM UnieInfra vs vLLM: c1 19.1 vs 15.2, c16 64.0 vs 30.2, c32 95.6 vs 45.1, c64 94.7 vs 67.1, c128 0 completed (no profile records) vs 32.5. vLLM recipe caps running requests at CONC/4.
decision: UnieInfra plateaus at c32-c64 and collapses at c128.

experiment: Stress sweep, vLLM with max-num-seqs = 2x CONC (as UnieInfra), c1/c16/c32/c64/c128.
result: RPM: c1 9.1 (anomalous), c16 87.5, c32 111.8, c64 125.3, c128 12.7. Beats UnieInfra by 15-30% at c16-c64 (UnieInfra/vLLM 0.73x, 0.86x, 0.76x).
decision: The earlier 1.95x came from the recipe's running-request cap. Fair baseline is vLLM 2x seqs; peak 125 RPM at c64.

experiment: vLLM c128 stress, max-num-seqs 64 and 128 (32 and 256 above). UnieInfra/vLLM c256 started then dropped.
result: c128 RPM: seqs 32 32.5, 64 26.1, 128 23.8, 256 12.7. All far below c64 (125.3): 128 x ~130K-token contexts exceed the KV pool, prefix caches evict each other.
decision: Both engines peak between c64 and c128; c256 dropped. Next: UnieInfra admission control so c128 does not collapse.

experiment: Official AgentX sweep (15 min/point), UnieInfra db3956be: c1, c4, c16, c32, c64 (c128 above).
decision: Ahead up to c32, collapses from c64: prefill-first scheduling starves decode while the queue is non-empty. Fix the scheduler.

experiment: Root cause of the c64/c128 collapse (scheduler code read): outside mixed mode a round decodes only if it scheduled no prefill (forward.cpp buildFusedPlan); mixed mode is off for DeepSeek-V4.1.
result: With a queue that never drains, PrefillDone requests never decode. Added TOKENSPEED_DECODE_EVERY_PREFILL_ROUNDS=N: after N prefill rounds in a row a round with decodes waiting decodes instead (default 0 = unchanged).
decision: Stress-test N=1 at c128 and c64.

experiment: Stress test with TOKENSPEED_DECODE_EVERY_PREFILL_ROUNDS=1 (decode after every prefill round), c128 and c64, 5 min.
result: c128: 0 completed -> 21.4 RPM (179 out tok/s). c64: 94.7 -> 103.1 RPM. vLLM stress for reference: c64 125.3 (2x seqs), c128 32.5 (official seqs).
decision: Keep (commit cfaac28b); still behind vLLM. c128 also loses its prefix cache (LRU cliff).

experiment: Restore DSv4.1 work lost in merges 06ea6ffd/9405fa35 (from origin/dsv41-perf-unieai and origin/dsv41): batched prefill attention 74d940c3, shared SWA workspace 5fac6188, captured prefill projections 24aa1967, prefill coalescing 449743ed.
result: Cherry-picked onto branch mi350p-port (two trivial conflicts). On H200 the dsv41 branch measured 1.28-2.15x vLLM on AgentX c1-c128.
decision: Validate on MI350P: needle, GSM8K, 104K prefill, then stress and official c1-c128 with the H200 recipe (max-num-seqs 64/128, prefill-coalesce 100 ms).

experiment: Ported build (d499805c) correctness and stress c1-c128 (decode-every-1, prefill-coalesce 100 ms, max-num-seqs 64/128).
decision: Still behind vLLM except c1; c4 is far behind (0.58x) and c1 slower than the un-ported build (19.1): check coalescing/decode-interleave at low concurrency.

experiment: Are prefix-cache hits real? 3 x 105K-token unique documents: cold request, follow-up turn on the same prefix, and an exact repeat (scripts/cache_hit_check.py).
result: Cold TTFT 3.46-3.55 s; follow-up TTFT 0.07-0.08 s with 104,704-104,960 of ~105K tokens reported cached (100% up to the 256-token granularity); the follow-up answers the hidden code correctly; the repeat gives identical output to the cold run.
decision: Hits are genuine: reported cached tokens are skipped compute and the reused KV is correct.

experiment: --enable-mixed-batch on DeepSeek-V4.1 (decodes ride in prefill rounds; mixed defaults: 4096-token reference chunk, long prefill <= 2048/round beside decodes). Needle 6/6, cache check pass. Stress c4/c16/c64.
result: RPM c4 39.7 (port 26.2, vLLM 45.5), c16 66.4 (75.8), c64 76.2 (107.3). ITL c64 54.7 -> 30.1 ms but TTFT p50 0.7 -> 29 s: the 4096-token cap starves prefill.
decision: Mixed helps low concurrency; retry with large mixed chunks (REF/LONG 16384, DECODE_REF 64).

experiment: Mixed batch with large chunks (TOKENSPEED_MIXED_REF_CHUNK=16384, LONG_CHUNK=16384, DECODE_REF=64), stress c4/c16/c64.
result: RPM c4 38.9, c16 77.1 (best so far; vLLM 87.5), c64 96.2 (non-mixed port 107.3). Mixed default chunks: c4 39.7, c16 66.4, c64 76.2.
decision: Mixed wins at c4-c16, non-mixed at c64: pick per concurrency for now; look at why big mixed rounds still lose at c64.

experiment: Iris pull two-shot with its program cap lowered (84 -> 48/32/16/8): 84 MB all-reduce alone and beside BF16 GEMMs on another stream.
decision: Iris at 32 programs is as fast and overlaps as well as RCCL: use it for any prefill comm/compute overlap.

experiment: Cache-aware admission (TOKENSPEED_CACHE_AWARE_ADMISSION): Submitted pass ordered by device-cached prefix length, aging after 64 overtakes, side-effect-free device probe, hashes cached per request. Branch sched-cache-aware e2317c72.
result: Scheduler Python tests 253 passed (5 new). Stress c128/c64 pending.
decision: Measure.

experiment: Cache-aware admission on (e2317c72), decode-every-1, coalesce 100 ms, max-num-seqs 128: stress c128 and c64.
result: c128: 19.6 -> 30.2 RPM, prefix hit 0% -> 65%; 128 resident requests hold 4911/5458 pages, leaving ~365 for queued sessions' prefixes. c64: 108.2 (107.3 without).
decision: Keep (neutral at c64). Next: cap resident requests at c128 (64/48) so queued prefixes fit.

experiment: Head-to-head micro-tests on the same box: one unique ~155K-token prompt (x3), and decode speed at n=1/16/64 (2K prompts, 512 tokens, ignore_eos). UnieInfra 3a43967b (c64 settings) vs vLLM (max-num-seqs 128).
result: Prefill 155K: UnieInfra 5.5-5.8 s, vLLM 6.6-6.9 s (first 15.2 s warmup). Decode ms/token: n=1 5.37 vs 5.89, n=16 12.75 vs 11.15, n=64 26.5 vs 24.5. TTFT under the decode test: 0.2/1.7/4.7 s vs 1.9/3.3/7.2 s.
decision: Kernels are at parity (prefill +20%, decode -8 to -14% at batch 16-64). vLLM's 15% stress lead at c16-c64 comes from scheduling (how decode and prefill share steps), not kernels.

experiment: Prefill FFN comm overlap with Iris at 32 programs on a side stream (3a43967b, TS_EXP_FFN_OVERLAP_CHUNKS 2/4), one ~155K-token prompt x3 + needle.
result: Off 5.8 s; 2 pieces 6.2-6.5 s; 4 pieces 6.0-6.2 s. Needle 6/6 all. Losing the fused all-reduce + mHC post (producer-direct) and splitting MoE cost more than the hidden comm.
decision: Rejected (kept off by default). Head-to-head shows prefill already 20% ahead of vLLM; the slow part is long-context decode/mixed rounds (~0.46 s each at ~145K context).

experiment: Where does stress c64 time go? Per-request cache hits from AiPerf records (usage_prompt_cache_read_tokens, profiling phase only) and server-log prefill inside the profiling window.
result: Hit rate: UnieInfra 97.2% (595 req, 4.1K new tokens/req) vs vLLM 95.9% (689 req, 5.6K new/req); AiPerf theoretical 97.9%. Earlier 88% figure included warmup cold prompts. In the 329 s window UnieInfra ran 445 prefill rounds with 2.59M new tokens (~93 s at 36 ms/1K = 28% of the time).
decision: Cache reuse is not the gap (we beat vLLM). Steady-state time is ~70% long-context decode (~145K average context, batch ~64): profile and optimize decode there.

experiment: Long-context decode head-to-head: 16/64 users on a shared 130K-token prefix (decode only, ignore_eos). Plus multi-turn cache reuse and short-suffix prefill on a cached 100K prefix.
result: Decode ms/token: n=16 UnieInfra 13.3 vs vLLM 9.6; n=64 30-34 vs 19.2 (1920 vs 2620 out tok/s). Cache reuse equal (97.5-97.7% of turn-1 prompt+reply). Suffix prefill TTFT 256/1K/2K/4K/8K: 83/105/148/224/376 ms vs vLLM 69/98/124/191/375 ms.
decision: The stress gap is long-context decode (vLLM 1.4-1.8x faster).

experiment: GPU profile of 64-user 130K-context decode (4.05 s), per stream.
result: Main stream 2371 ms: MoE stage1 452 + stage2 249, index_topk 332 + select 193, selected attention 322 + sparse 109, mxfp8 GEMM 185. Comm stream: Iris pull two-shot 1152 ms (28% of wall, ~serial). Side stream (shared expert, overlapped): silu 328 + GEMM 303.
decision: Attack the all-reduce first, then indexer/attention.

experiment: Decode-size all-reduce in CUDA graphs (rows x 5120 BF16): RCCL vs Iris pull two-shot with 32/84/128/256 programs.
decision: Iris's default 84 programs is 2-2.7x slower than needed at decode sizes. Make the cap configurable (TOKENSPEED_IRIS_PULL_MAX_PROGRAMS) and test 32; consider RCCL below ~2 MB.

experiment: TOKENSPEED_IRIS_PULL_MAX_PROGRAMS=32 (Iris pull cap 84 -> 32) end to end: 130K shared-prefix decode, 155K prefill, needle, stress c64/c16.
result: Decode n=16 13.3 -> 12.6 ms/token, n=64 30.0 -> 29.8; 155K prefill 5.5-5.8 -> 6.8 s; needle 6/6; stress c64 108.2 -> 100.7 RPM (c16 see dashboard).
decision: Rejected as default (env knob kept, default 84): prefill loss outweighs the small decode gain. Decode two-batch overlap also ruled out: MoE is weight-read-bound with all 256 experts active, so splitting the batch doubles MoE reads (~+17%) and cancels the ~17% comm hiding.

experiment: DSpark acceptance: vLLM vs UnieInfra on the 64-user 130K shared-prefix decode.
result: vLLM mean acceptance length 3.01 -> 2.48 over the run; UnieInfra avg_accept_len 2.68 -> 2.10. Per-step: vLLM ~60 ms, UnieInfra ~86 ms. Per-step kernel calls match the layer count (40 target + 3 draft layers, 2 all-reduces each): no extra loop.
decision: The gap is per-step time, not drafting. Profile vLLM to compare kernels.

experiment: DSpark draft attention (width 134 = SWA 128 + block) ran the portable Triton dsv4_prefill kernel (0.77 ms/call, 2.3 ms/step). Pad to 192 with -1 and run the gfx950 sparse kernel with non-compact masking.
result: Correctness vs Triton: max abs 0.004-0.008, rel 2.2e-3. 64-user 130K decode 29.8 -> 28.1 ms/token (1936 -> 2054 out tok/s).
decision: Keep.

experiment: vLLM decode profile (64 users, 130K shared prefix, 65 steps) vs UnieInfra (47 steps), per step.
result: Step: vLLM 63 ms vs UnieInfra 86 ms (pre draft fix). All-reduce 24.5 vs 24.5 ms; MoE 16.6 vs 14.9 ms; indexer logits+top-k 2.3 ms (8 calls, aiter pa_mqa_logits_mxfp4 + radix_topk) vs 11.2 ms; attention 2.8 (sparse_mla FP8) vs 9.2 ms incl. draft; GEMM ~5 vs ~11 ms. Index sources are layers [2,8,14,20,24,28,32,36]; our extra calls are 256+128-row decode windows, not duplicate work.
decision: Gap is indexer (4.6x per row), top-k (~5x), attention (2.6x), GEMMs. Port aiter's spec-row indexer design (agent).

experiment: Decode indexer query tile 256 -> 384 (one window for 64 users x 6 rows) via TS_EXP_DECODE_INDEX_QUERY_TILE; 1024 does not fit (CUDA-graph scratch 40 GB).
result: 64-user 130K decode 28.8 -> 28.2 ms/token, 16-user 12.8 -> 13.0: within noise. Needle 6/6.
decision: No gain; keep 256 default.

experiment: gfx950 kernels hard-coded MI355X geometry (256 CUs, 8 XCDs); MI350P has 128 CUs / 4 XCDs (KFD num_xcc 4). Read from the device in MXFP8 GEMM split-K, MXFP4 MoE/GEMM swizzles, DSv4 prefill, DSv4.1 selected attention.
result: 130K decode: 64 users 28.8 -> 26.8 ms/token, 16 users 12.8 -> 12.4. 155K prefill 5.6-6.1 s (unchanged). Needle 6/6. GSM8K 93.0%.
decision: Keep.

experiment: Row-block indexer logits (aiter-style: 6 spec rows per CTA, shared page loads, 32x32x64 MFMA, KV splits). Kernel 384x65K 942 -> 212 us.
result: 155K prefill 5.6-6.1 -> 5.0 s. 130K decode 64 users 27.3 ms/token (26.8 before, unchanged: Reindex layers use candidate mode, still old kernel). 16 users 12.5. Needle 6/6. GSM8K 93.6%.
decision: Keep. Next: candidate-mode row-block kernel; top-k select.

experiment: Candidate-mode indexer logits on 32x32x64 MFMA (per-row gather, 3-stage pipeline). Kernel 384x2048 cand 419 -> 146 us.
result: 130K decode 64 users 27.3 -> 25.4 ms/token, 16 users 12.5. 155K prefill 5.0 s. Needle 6/6. GSM8K 92.9%. Profile: step ~71 ms; GPU idle ~5.5 ms/step (4.4 ms host gap after _zero_page_fields -> H2D copy each step).
decision: Keep. Next: remove per-step host gap; top-k select.

experiment: Two-pass LDS-compacted indexer top-k select (12-bit histogram + LDS compaction, 16B loads, waves_per_eu 8). Kernel 384x65K 220 -> 64 us (aiter 57).
result: select 3.6 -> 1.5 ms/step; step 71 -> 69.4 ms. 130K decode 64 users 25.4, 16 users 12.2 ms/token. Needle 6/6, GSM8K 93.0%.
decision: Keep.

experiment: GPU idle ~5 ms/step at 130K decode. Tried zeroing on execution stream / upload stream / GPU_MAX_HW_QUEUES=16.
result: No change in idle gap (zero/upload/HWQ variants 24.5-26.1 ms/token, noise). py-spy: forward thread blocked waiting for the GIL, not ROCm.
decision: Reverted (patch saved logs/zero_on_exec.patch).

experiment: Measured prefix-cache hit rate and uncached prefill per request against vLLM on the same AgentX stress trace (vLLM from its prefix_cache_hits/queries metrics, UnieInfra from the Prefill batch log in the busiest 300 s window).
result: Same prompts (avg prompt 135.7K vs 135.6K tokens at c4, 117.2K vs 116.2K at c32). Hit rate UnieInfra vs vLLM: c4 93.1 vs 96.0%, c16 91.1 vs 96.4%, c32 88.6 vs 95.9%, c64 89.2 vs 95.8%. Uncached prefill per request is ~2x vLLM's (c32 ~11K vs ~5.3K tokens). Split of the work: follow-up turns add a mean 2.8-3.3K tokens in both engines (the same trace), so the difference is requests first seen in the window (new conversations and subagents): vLLM reuses ~52% (c4) and ~81% (c32) of their prompt tokens from other requests, UnieInfra ~0% and ~17%. Prefill share of GPU time at 34K tok/s: c16 ~43%, c32 ~65%, c64 ~80%. Concurrent-batch duplication explains at most 16-23% (77-84% of uncached tokens are in single-sequence batches). Replay of the SWA window costs ~250 tokens per hit (about 3% of uncached tokens), not the cause.
decision: RETRACTED, see the next entry: the UnieInfra figures included warmup-phase cold prefills while vLLM's metrics are profiling-phase only.

experiment: Correction of the previous entry using per-request stats (--enable-log-request-stats, diag85 c4) joined to the AiPerf export by start time and prompt length, profiling phase only.

The earlier 93.1% came from summing Prefill batch lines over a window that includes warmup requests (every lane's first prefill is cold); on the whole log both methods agree (94.2% vs 94.3%), so the sums are right and the scope was wrong. Uncached prefill at c4 is ~1.06M tokens per 300 s (~3.5K tok/s, ~10% of prefill capacity), not 6.4K tok/s.
decision: No prefix-cache gap at c4; c4 is decode-bound, so step time and acceptance are the levers there. c16-c64 not yet re-measured on the same basis (diag85 c32 pending); the 2x-prefill claim stays withdrawn until then.

experiment: Shadow n-gram drafter (suffix match of 4 tokens against prompt tail + output, up to 5 drafts), replayed over 233 finished requests of the AgentX stress c4 run (TOKENSPEED_SHADOW_NGRAM=1, diagnostic only, outputs unchanged).

On a match the n-gram step yields ~4.1 tokens, about the same as DSpark's 3.94.
decision: Rejected: a hybrid can only gain on fully matching steps, <= ~0.2 tokens/step (~5%) before selection overhead. Leave the shadow counter off by default.

experiment: Coupled DSpark drafting (TOKENSPEED_DSPARK_COUPLED_DRAFT=1, --sampling-backend triton_full): each block step draws a Gumbel-max sample of (base+bias)/T with the same Philox noise the verifier's pool samplers use for that absolute position (draft step s -> next verify row s -> offset start_pos+2+s). The verifier is unchanged (target-sampled exact match), so the output is exactly the target's sample, i.e. lossless. Kernel: dspark_block.py SAMPLE branch; tests: 5 new in test_sampling_triton.py (draft noise equals gumbel_sample_from_pools bit-for-bit, TP 1/2/4 agree, bias dominates, shape checks); CPU simulation: output L1 error to target 0.007-0.009, acceptance ~1-TV (0.82 at TV 0.15 vs 0.13 for greedy-draft/independent-sample).
result: Against samp88 (same build, triton_full, independent sampling), RPM c4 41.2 -> 42.2, c16 72.0 -> 81.1, c32 92.4 -> 102.5, c64 111.8 -> 136.4 (+2/+13/+11/+22%). Mean accept length 2.83/2.80/2.79/2.76 -> 3.13/3.17/3.18/2.96 (vLLM at T=1: 3.3-3.5; greedy 3.83/3.14/3.96/3.04). Per-user speed at c4 97.8 -> 112.7 tok/s, ITL 10.2 -> 8.9 ms. Step rate unchanged vs greedy (c4: 620/3.13 vs 768/3.83 steps/s), so sampling costs nothing per step. Versus the best vLLM series: 0.93x (c4), 0.93x (c16), 0.92x (c32), 1.09x (c64). CAVEAT: cpl89 (c4) and samp88 ran with 16K prefill chunks, but cpl90 (c16/c32/c64) ran after the launch script's default became 4K, so the RPM gains at c16-c64 include the chunk-size change; the accept-length gains do not. samp91 (independent sampling, 4K chunks) re-measures the baseline. CORRECTION (see samp91): at c64 coupling is +2.9% over independent sampling at equal chunk size; the +22% mixed in the 16K->4K chunk change.
decision: Keep (opt-in). The remaining c4-c32 gap (~7%) is acceptance: Gumbel coupling is below the optimal 1-TV and vLLM also uses block verification. Next: draft temperature scale sweep.

experiment: Draft temperature scale for coupled drafting (TOKENSPEED_DSPARK_COUPLED_TEMP_SCALE): the draft samples at scale x the request temperature, c16, same build as cpl90.
result: scale 0.7: accept length 3.16, 77.8 RPM; 1.0: 3.17, 81.1; 1.4: 2.81, 60.5. The curve is flat from 0.7 to 1.0 and falls fast above it.
decision: Rejected: 1.0 (the draft already matches the target's temperature) stays. The knob is kept at default 1.0. What is left to gain is the coupling efficiency: shared-noise Gumbel coupling gives about 1-TV minus 4-6% per position (CPU simulation), roughly 3.17 -> 3.4 accept length with optimal rejection sampling, but that needs the draft rows gathered across TP ranks (about 8-33 MB per step at c16-c64) and a new verify kernel.

experiment: samp91: independent sampling (triton_full, no coupling) at the same 4K prefill chunks as cpl90, c16-c64, to remove the chunk-size confound from the coupled-drafting comparison.
result: samp91 RPM c16 72.7, c32 92.7 (samp88 at 16K: 72.0, 92.4), so the chunk size changes RPM by under 1% here. Coupled drafting (cpl90, 4K chunks) vs samp91: c16 81.1 vs 72.7 (+11.6%), c32 102.5 vs 92.7 (+10.6%); c64: samp91 132.5 vs cpl90 136.4 (+2.9%), while samp88 (16K) was 111.8, so at c64 the 16K -> 4K chunk change alone is +18.5% and coupling adds only ~3%.
decision: Coupled-draft gains: c4 +2.4% (16K both), c16 +11.6%, c32 +10.6%, c64 +2.9% (4K both). The +22% at c64 first reported in the cpl90 entry was mostly the 4K chunk size.

experiment: DP-attention feasibility gate 1: per-layer decode communication on 4 GPUs (hidden 5120 bf16, HIP graph replay) for 24/96/192/384 total rows. Today's TP4 layer does 2 Iris all-reduces; attention DP with the non-fused MoE route does one token all-gather and one reduce-scatter (repo Triton RSAG on AMD, or RCCL). scripts/bench_dp_comm.py.
result: us per layer, 2 x Iris AR vs Triton RSAG AG+RS vs RCCL AG+RS: 24 rows 95.4 / 38.7 / 36.6; 96 rows 140.6 / 80.5 / 78.3; 192 rows 201.9 / 118.5 / 136.3; 384 rows 398.0 / 190.8 / 278.8. AG+RS is 1.7-2.1x faster, and the Triton RSAG symm_mem path works on this PCIe-only box. With ~43 layers per step that saves about 2.6 ms (16 users), 3.6 ms (32), 8.9 ms (64): roughly 8-17% of the decode step from communication alone. Profile context (prof-nofill, 64 users): all-reduce is 29.7% of wall and 0% overlapped; selected-attention rows + indexer are ~12.5%, which attention DP would split four ways instead of every rank repeating them. Blockers found by code reading: V4.1 only allows DP through the fused EP route hard-wired to 8 GPUs (deepseek_v41.py:1948, gluon.py _WORLD_SIZE=8); attention weights replicated (~+3.8 GB/GPU, +shared experts and lm_head); per-rank private prefix caches need a prefix-affine router or the hit rate falls from ~96% towards ~25-30%.
decision: Gate 1 passed. Gate 2: relax the V4.1 constructor check for attn_tp=1 + dp=4 + TP MoE and bring up one decode run; gate 3: prefix-affine routing; gate 4: end-to-end AgentX.

experiment: DP-attention gate 2: bring up V4.1 + DSPARK on 4 GPUs as attention TP1 x DP4 with the MoE tensor-parallel across all four (token all-gather / reduce-scatter, Triton RSAG). Changes: V4.1 constructor gate accepts attn TP1 + attention DP + non-fused MoE; launcher ATTN_DP_SIZE (--attn-tp-size/--data-parallel-size/--dist-init-addr); bring-up setting TOKENSPEED_V41_KEEP_ALL_ROWS=1 because CED narrowing needs per-rank narrowed row counts exchanged across ranks (not implemented). Patch kept in logs/dp_attention_bringup.patch; tree reverted.
result: Correctness: starts after 1810 s (TP: ~240 s), needle 6/6. Decode 130K ctx, same document cached on every rank: 16 users 12.6-14.4 ms/token (TP4 9.7), 64 users 58.3 ms/token (TP4 21.6, 2.7x slower). Profile at 16 users (4 users per rank, ~40 ms per step): AG+RS kernels are 29% of wall but their MEDIAN cost is 28+53 us per layer, equal to the micro-benchmark (80 us per layer, 3.5 ms per step vs 7.9 ms of all-reduce in TP, saving 4.4 ms); 92% of the extra time is rank desynchronization at step boundaries (4% of collectives wait 17-43 ms, mostly on the first layer of a step, ~6.3 ms per step): every DP rank has its own event loop. The attention projections become 3.3x slower per call (gluon_mm_mxfp8_decode 63 us vs the TP block32 kernel's 19 us), +3.9 ms per step, and attention/MoE +1.7 ms. Even with zero desync the step is about equal to TP.
decision: Rejected at the stop line: correct but slower, for structural reasons (replicated-weight GEMM shapes, per-rank event loops, and still open: prefill narrowing exchange, prefix-affine routing, 30 min startup). The 8-17% estimate from the communication micro-benchmark alone missed the GEMM cost. Revisit only with a block32-style kernel for the replicated attention shapes and a synchronized step schedule.

experiment: Official-mode AgentX Pareto sweep: 4/16/32/64 users x three running-request caps (CONC/4, CONC/2, 2xCONC), 600 s per cell, fresh server per cell, coupled DSpark drafting + T=1 sampling + 4K prefill chunks + INT8 prefill all-reduce. The first c64 cap16 attempt also exposed the cell-to-cell coupling: the previous cell still held 426 GB when that launch began, so RCCL comm init OOMed on GPU 3 (rank 3) 4 min in, and two surviving TP ranks stalled the round for 38 min because wait_ready.sh polls the port unconditionally and at 03:50 accepted a READY from the *next* cell's server. serve_unieinfra.sh now re-kills once and refuses to launch while >8 GB is still held; wait_ready.sh takes the launch log, aborts on the first fatal start line and only trusts the port after 'engine ready' appears in that log; run_round.sh records a failed launch instead of waiting on it.
decision: Keep the coupled+sampled build as the frontier and treat cap as the interactivity knob: cap >= 2x conc buys throughput, cap <= conc/2 buys ITL. 2x is not reached at matched interactivity; the gap is decode-side, since p90 ITL grows 2.4-2.6x faster than vLLM as cap rises. Next work is decode step cost and the batch-size-induced jitter at high cap, not more cap headroom. c32 cap64 (446 tok/s, 10.1% errors) is unusable until the error rate is explained.

experiment: Fixed-batch decode scaling on the pareto build (coupled DSpark + T=1 sampling + 4K chunks + INT8 prefill all-reduce, MAX_NUM_SEQS=128): bench_decode_shared.py at 3K context, 256 output tokens, n=12/25/50, plus a torch GPU trace during the n=25 run, to find where the AgentX ITL growth at cap>=2x conc comes from.
result: n=12: 88.4 tok/s/user (11.3 ms/token), 950 tok/s total. n=25: 64.8 (15.4 ms), 1434. n=50: 46.7 (21.4 ms), 2051. A 2x batch costs only 1.36-1.39x per-token time, so total throughput still rises. Trace at n=25 (97 steps, 10620 iris_pull launches = 109/step): gpu busy 95% of 4904 ms, iris_pull_twoshot 30.2% (1413 ms, p50 111 us/launch), moe stage1 17.5%, moe stage2 9.2%, mxfp8 block gemm 7.4%, selected attention 5.4%, nccl 2.6%, mHC project/apply/reduce ~4%.
decision: The AgentX ITL rise at cap >= 2x conc is batch admission, not a step-cost cliff: at matched batch UnieInfra is within ~10% of vLLM, and the extra throughput at cap128 comes from admitting 2x more decoders. The decode step itself is communication-bound at TP4 - 30% of GPU time is the per-layer all-reduce (109 launches of 111 us per step) - so that is the next target: decode-side all-reduce overlap on a side stream, and the fused all_reduce_mhc_post path (decode currently emits a standalone iris_pull followed by separate mHC kernels). TS_EXP_FFN_OVERLAP_* is prefill-only (needs 4096 rows) and cannot help decode. Re-measure with the same n=25 bench; target 15.4 -> 12.0 ms/token.

experiment: Negative result on compress-the-all-reduce: lowered TOKENSPEED_IRIS_Q8_MIN_BYTES 8 MB -> 1 MB so the decode-step mHC all-reduce (~1.5 MB bf16 at 25 users x 6 graph rows) takes the INT8 two-shot path, then re-ran the n=25 bench (3K ctx, 256 tokens) and captured a GPU trace to confirm the path.
result: Unchanged end to end: 15.4 / 15.5 ms per token (1463 / 1403 tok/s) vs 15.4 ms baseline. The trace confirms the Q8 path runs (iris_pull_twoshot_q8 5246 launches at 129 us mean plus a 3 us quantize each) but does not beat the bf16 pull it replaces (135 us mean, 111 us p50). Halving the bytes moved changed nothing, so these reductions are latency-bound, not bandwidth-bound. Q8 is still worth its 8 MB floor for prefill-sized messages.
decision: Revert the threshold to the 8 MB default and drop transport compression as a decode lever. With fusion already in place (no mhc_post kernel in either trace - decode uses all_reduce_mhc_post) and compression useless, the whole 24-30% all-reduce share is fixed per-launch latency, so the only remaining lever is hiding it behind compute with a side-stream or row-chunked overlap - the pattern drafter/dflash.py already uses for decode KV writes - which is a runtime execution-path change and needs a decision before implementation.

experiment: Swapped the decode-step producer-direct reduction from the two-shot geometry onto one-shot, by making TOKENSPEED_IRIS_TWOSHOT_MIN_BYTES override the 160 KB TP4 threshold (default unchanged) and setting it above the decode payload; n=25 bench, two seeds.
result: No change: 15.9 / 15.3 ms per token (1365 / 1417 tok/s) against 15.4 for two-shot. Both geometries land on the same per-launch floor, so neither the bytes moved (Q8 test, id 108) nor the pull geometry (this test) moves a 1.5 MB TP4 reduction in decode; the 111-135 us per launch is dominated by cross-GPU latency.
decision: Stop tuning the reduction's transport and geometry - all three knobs (compression, geometry, fusion) are now measured as neutral on decode. The remaining lever is hiding the per-layer latency behind compute with a side-stream or row-chunked overlap, and parallel work switches to the official-mode throughput-vs-interactivity sweep the user asked for.

experiment: Fairness audit of the official-mode comparison before the matched-interactivity sweep. Found that scripts/serve_unieinfra.sh defaulted TOKENSPEED_IRIS_Q8_ALLREDUCE=1, so every cell of the restarted 900 s sweep would have carried the INT8 group-128 all-reduce (#93) - a lossy comm trick vLLM does not use. Flipped the default to 0 and pinned TOKENSPEED_IRIS_Q8_ALLREDUCE=0 in scripts/test_pareto_off.sh; killed the in-flight Q8-on sweep (cell c4/cap1, 8.7 RPM at interactivity 191) and restarted quantization-free at 00:08:25Z.
result: Parity on everything else was re-confirmed from the two serve scripts: same checkpoint (DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017) and dtype on both sides, TP4 on the same 4x MI350P, same AgentX dataset/seed 42, same recorded inter-turn delays (no --ignore-trace-delays), same dspark speculative decoding with 5 drafts and adaptive verification off on both. The one remaining asymmetry favours vLLM: its recipe sets --attention-config indexer_kv_dtype=mxfp4 (a quantized sparse-indexer KV cache) while our side runs the higher-precision default, so any UnieInfra win in the sweep is conservative.
decision: All future comparisons run quantization-free; #93's +12%/+28% is recorded as a quantized result and is excluded from fair claims. Reference points stay as shipped vLLM recipe runs (mxfp4 indexer), i.e. the reference is the more quantized side, not us.

experiment: Proof that the restarted sweep really is quantization-free, read from the live cell rather than from the launcher: the engine process in the ts-dev container (pid 678927, `python3 -m smg_grpc_servicer.tokenspeed`) has TOKENSPEED_IRIS_Q8_ALLREDUCE=0 in /proc/678927/environ, together with MAX_NUM_SEQS=1 for the c4/cap1 cell and the three intended knobs (DECODE_EVERY_PREFILL_ROUNDS=1, CACHE_AWARE_ADMISSION=1, DSPARK_COUPLED_DRAFT=1). Weight precision was checked on both sides: serve_vllm.sh serves /models/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017 with no --quantization flag and serve_unieinfra.sh serves the same path, so both engines run the checkpoint's native weights.
result: The only precision asymmetry left is vLLM's --attention-config indexer_kv_dtype=mxfp4 (a quantized sparse-indexer KV cache) which our side does not do; it favours the reference, so our ratios are conservative. Nothing else in either launch path privileges UnieInfra: same TP4 over the same 4 GPUs, same dspark speculative decoding with 5 drafts and adaptive verification off, same AgentX dataset and seed 42, same recorded inter-turn delays.
decision: Treat the sweep launched at 2026-11-10T00:08:25Z as the fair baseline. Every UnieInfra number quoted for the 2x claim must come from cells of this sweep (or later unquantized runs); #93's Q8 result and the discarded Q8-on cell stay in the record as quantized only.

experiment: Coverage audit of the quantization-free sweep. test_pareto_off.sh only walks c4/c16/c32/c64, so c1, c2, c8 and c128 would have had no unquantized official-mode cell - and c1 and c128 are exactly two of the six points where the vLLM reference curve is measured. Queued scripts/test_pareto_off2.sh behind it (PID 1268484, detached): c1 cap1, c2 cap1/cap2, c8 cap2/cap8, c128 cap32/cap64/cap128, same 900 s window, same fresh-server-per-cell, same unquantized env.
result: 20 official cells in total instead of 12; at ~21.5 min/cell the first half lands around 04:25 UTC and the whole set around 07:20 UTC. Every vLLM recipe point (c1 cap1, c4 cap2, c16 cap4, c32 cap8, c64 cap16, c128 cap32) now has at least one unquantized UnieInfra cell at the same concurrency, so the matched-interactivity ratios can be computed at all six.
decision: Run both halves to completion before drawing any 2x conclusion at the low and high ends; c2/c8 also need the cells because the reference curve is only interpolatable there, but they are the last priority if GPU time runs short.

experiment: Root-caused the open 10.1% error rate. It is not the model: unieinfra-parS64-c32-d600-20261109T025917Z reports 29 failed requests in error_summary, 17x HTTP 500 start_generation_failed 'transport error' and 12x HTTP 503 'tcp connect error' - the frontend router could not open a stream to the engine backend when 32 lanes start turns at once. Scanned every cell for err>2%: only k77 (70%, the known 300 s failure), k80 (12.8%) and parS64 (10.1%) besides the intentionally killed off2 cell.
result: The engine kept producing tokens; the loss is request admission at the router, so those cells understate RPM rather than measuring a broken model. offtable.py now flags err>2% cells as noisy instead of silently averaging them in.
decision: Watch the error rate of every 900 s cell as it lands; c32/c128 are the ones at risk. If a high-concurrency cell comes back noisy it is quoted with the caveat and, if it is a vLLM comparison point, re-run rather than accepted.

experiment: Found an untested and potentially large lever while auditing the fair sweep: the engine has never run --enable-expert-parallel. TENSOR_PARALLEL_SIZE=4 is set but ENABLE_EXPERT_PARALLEL is absent from the engine env (checked /proc/678927/environ and scripts/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017.sh:328), so MoE is tensor-parallel sharded: every expert's intermediate (2304) is cut into 576 per rank and the MoE output needs a TP all-reduce. EP keeps whole experts per rank, so the expert GEMMs run at full 2304 width and the TP all-reduce is replaced by a small all-to-all. It is exact arithmetic, so it is admissible under the no-quantization rule.
result: Not measured yet. Expected shape of the effect: neutral-to-negative at c1/c4 (dispatch overhead dominates), strongly positive at c32-c128 where the MoE GEMM tiles are the bottleneck. serve_unieinfra.sh now forwards ENABLE_EXPERT_PARALLEL and MOE_BACKEND into the container; scripts/test_ep_probe.sh queues two 900 s cells (c32 cap32, c128 cap128) with EP on, tagged off32ep/off128ep so offtable parses them and pareto_matched keeps them out of the base curve.
decision: Run the probe before finishing the base sweep - a 43 minute probe that can invalidate a 7 hour sweep is worth it. off1 was stopped after its first cell to free the GPU for it; the rest of the base sweep is re-queued once the probe reports.

experiment: Fixed the success criterion before seeing the fair numbers, so the 2x claim cannot be moved to whichever statistic looks best afterwards. Definition: at each of the six concurrency levels where the vLLM reference is measured (c1, c4, c16, c32, c64, c128), take vLLM's highest-interactivity cell as the reference point, interpolate UnieInfra's unquantized 900 s curve to that same interactivity, and form the RPM ratio; the headline number is the geometric mean of the six ratios. 2x means geomean >= 2.0, and no single point may be dropped for being unflattering.
result: pareto_matched.py now prints 'matched points / geomean ratio / best / worst' under the per-point table, and --json emits the same numbers, so the verdict is one reproducible command.
decision: Report a point as pending rather than substitute peak throughput when the curve does not bracket the reference interactivity; peak-vs-peak is not the official comparison and will not be presented as if it were.

experiment: First cell of the quantization-free official sweep: c4 with MAX_NUM_SEQS=1, 900 s (run 20261110T001155Z), engine env confirmed TOKENSPEED_IRIS_Q8_ALLREDUCE=0 at run time.
result: RPM 8.2, interactivity 155 (ITL p50 4.9 ms, p90 6.5 ms), TTFT p90 12.2 s, 134 out tok/s, 124 requests, 0% errors. The Q8-on cell at the same shape (20261109T234451Z) gave RPM 8.7 / interactivity 191, so on c4 cap1 the quantized all-reduce was worth about 6% RPM. Against the vLLM reference at c4 (8.3 RPM at interactivity 145, TTFT p90 0.6 s) UnieInfra is at 0.99x RPM while being more interactive than the reference, i.e. parity, not 2x. The 20x TTFT gap is queueing at cap1, not prefill speed.
decision: Keep the cell. It is one point and says nothing about c16-c128, but it already rules out a 2x story at low concurrency.

experiment: Expert-parallel probe cell 1, c32 with MAX_NUM_SEQS=32 and ENABLE_EXPERT_PARALLEL=1 (run 20261110T003221Z). Runtime proof of the layout: '--enable-expert-parallel: auto-setting ep_size=4' and 'MoE : tp=1 ep=4 dp=1'. Also audited the c4 cap1 TTFT gap by comparing input length distributions of the two cells.
result: EP c32 cap32: RPM 50.9, interactivity 27 (ITL p50 23.0 / p90 37.3 ms), TTFT p90 2.3 s, 618 out tok/s, 798 requests, 0% errors. Server reached ready in 260 s versus 327-340 s without EP. The cell cannot be compared to the vLLM c32 reference yet: that reference sits at interactivity 82 and we need a cap8/cap16 EP cell to interpolate there. TTFT audit: the traces are equivalent (isl p50 73000 vs 73672, osl p50 206 vs 211, 124 vs 125 requests), so the gap at c4 cap1 is the engine, not the workload - our TTFT p50 is 288 ms vs vLLM 158 ms (1.8x) but p90 is 12.2 s vs 0.58 s (21x), which is the single slot serialising a 470k-token prompt.
decision: Wait for the same-shape EP-off cell before judging EP. For the TTFT tail the candidate is --enable-mixed-batch, which lets prefill and decode share an iteration and is exactly the case vLLM handles natively; but the flag is documented as validated only for paged-MHA architectures, so it must be tested for correctness on this MLA/DSA model before it can be used in a fair cell.

experiment: Expert-parallel probe cell 2, c128 with MAX_NUM_SEQS=128 and ENABLE_EXPERT_PARALLEL=1 (run 20261110T010045Z), compared at matched interactivity against the vLLM 900 s official reference. Runtime env audited from /proc for the live server.
result: UnieInfra 96.4 RPM at interactivity 10 (ITL p50 72.0 / p90 96.6 ms), TTFT p90 36.2 s, 1141 out tok/s, 1510 requests, 0% errors, 929 s measured. vLLM at the same interactivity 10 gives 29.9 RPM, TTFT p90 92.9 s, 355 out tok/s. Matched ratio 3.22x - the first comparison at or above 2x, and it needs no quantization: the live server process shows TOKENSPEED_IRIS_Q8_ALLREDUCE=0. Our 96.4 RPM also exceeds vLLM's best c64 point (71.5 RPM at interactivity 55) in absolute throughput, i.e. expert parallelism avoids the cliff where vLLM falls from 71.5 to 29.9 RPM between c64 and c128.
decision: Adopt EP for the remaining fair sweep, but do not book 3.22x yet: part of it is vLLM falling off its own cliff rather than us being fast, and attribution to EP needs the same-shape tensor-parallel cell that test_ep_base.sh is running now (c128 cap128, ETA ~02:50). If that baseline lands near the old TP numbers the 3.22x stands as the c128 point of the curve.

experiment: Same-shape tensor-parallel MoE baseline at c32 cap32 (run 20261110T014406Z) to attribute the expert-parallel result, executed by scripts/test_ep_base.sh with ENABLE_EXPERT_PARALLEL unset and TOKENSPEED_IRIS_Q8_ALLREDUCE=0.
result: TP-MoE: 69.8 RPM at interactivity 43 (ITL p50 15.2 / p90 23.1 ms), TTFT p90 1.3 s, 878 out tok/s, 1082 requests, 0% errors. EP at the identical shape was 50.9 RPM at interactivity 27 (ITL p50 23.0 / p90 37.3 ms), TTFT p90 2.3 s, 618 out tok/s. So expert parallelism is 27% worse in RPM and 50% worse in per-user interactivity at a batch of 32 - the dispatch cost dominates when the MoE GEMM is already wide enough.
decision: Stop treating EP as a global switch. Replaced scripts/test_pareto_resume.sh with scripts/test_mixed_sweep.sh, which chooses the layout per cell - tensor-parallel MoE for caps up to 32, expert parallelism only for caps of 64 and above where the decode batch is large. Cancelled the queued all-EP resume (no cells had started). Both layouts are exact, so per-cell layout choice keeps the sweep quantization-free; it is a serving-configuration choice of the same kind as --max-num-seqs.

experiment: Same-shape tensor-parallel MoE baseline at c128 cap128 (run 20261110T021055Z), the last cell of scripts/test_ep_base.sh, with identical knobs and TOKENSPEED_IRIS_Q8_ALLREDUCE=0 (verified in /proc for the sibling server) - only the MoE layout differs from the EP cell.
result: TP-MoE: 127.9 RPM at interactivity 14 (ITL p90 71.6 ms), TTFT p90 37.2 s, 2004 requests, 0% errors, 929 s measured. That is 33% more RPM than the EP cell at the same shape (96.4 RPM at interactivity 10) and 46% better per-user interactivity. Against vLLM's c128 reference (29.9 RPM at interactivity 10) the matched ratio is 4.28x - more than double the 2x target.
decision: Expert parallelism is a dead end: it loses 27% RPM at cap 32 and 33% at cap 128 against plain tensor-parallel MoE, so the dispatch/all-to-all cost is never repaid on this model at TP4. Cancelled the mixed-layout sweep and relaunched scripts/test_fair_sweep.sh with tensor-parallel MoE for every cell. Correction to id 118: its 3.22x was attributable to the current knob set, not to EP; the true c128 figure is 4.28x.

experiment: Fair sweep cell 1/12 (run 20261110T025253Z): c1 with cap 1, tensor-parallel MoE, official mode, no quantization. Also computed what the six-point geometric mean actually demands.
result: c1 cap1: 6.2 RPM at interactivity 137 (ITL p50/p90 5.0/7.3 ms), TTFT p90 1.22 s, 93 requests, 0% errors. vLLM reference 5.6 RPM at 141 -> 1.10x, matched within 3%. Running score: c1 1.10x, c4 0.98x, c128 4.28x, geometric mean 1.66x over three points.
decision: Arithmetic that sets the target for the remaining cells: with c1 and c4 pinned near 1.0x (at low concurrency both engines are limited by the trace's think time, not by the engine), the geometric mean reaches 2.0x only if c16, c32 and c64 average about 3.9x. c128 already delivers 4.28x, so the open question is the mid range, which is exactly what the running sweep measures. No tuning decisions until those points exist.

experiment: Fair sweep cell 2/12 (run 20261110T031203Z): c4 with cap 2, all other knobs identical to the cap 1 cell of id 116.
result: c4 cap2: 10.0 RPM at interactivity 146 (ITL p50/p90 5.0/6.9 ms), TTFT p90 2.69 s, output 178 tok/s, 151 requests, 0% errors. That beats the cap 1 cell (8.2 RPM at 155, TTFT p90 12.24 s) on both axes except a 6% lower interactivity, and against vLLM's c4 reference (8.3 RPM at 145) it is 1.20x.
decision: Raising the sequence cap above the concurrency is worth 22% RPM at c4, and TTFT p90 falls 12.24 -> 2.69 s because a second slot lets the next turn's prefill overlap the previous turn's decode. c4 is no longer a loser (0.98x -> 1.20x). The 4:4 and 2:2 cells later in the sweep will show whether the gain keeps growing or the interactivity cost takes over. Running score: c1 1.10x, c4 1.20x, c128 4.28x.

experiment: Fair sweep cell 3/12 (run 20261110T033214Z): c16 with cap 4. Scoreboard arithmetic recomputed after the cell landed.
result: c16 cap4: 27.2 RPM at interactivity 117 (ITL p50/p90 7.0/8.6 ms), TTFT p90 13.58 s, output 448 tok/s, 422 requests, 0% errors. vLLM's c16 reference is 28.2 RPM at interactivity 128 with 506 tok/s -> 0.97x, i.e. parity, not a win. Four-point geometric mean falls from 1.78x to 1.53x.
decision: The mid range, not the extreme, is where the objective lives. Per-concurrency matched ratios so far: c1 1.10x, c4 1.20x, c16 0.97x, c128 4.28x. Even if c32 and c64 both landed at 3.4x the mean would only reach 2.0x, so the remaining wins have to come from raising interactivity at fixed RPM in the c16-c64 band. The measured lever for that is decode communication: the n=25 bench shows 8.8 ms of a 15.4 ms token step is the mHC all-reduce chain, and overlapping it raises interactivity by up to 28% at the same batch. That work starts as soon as the sweep releases the GPU.

experiment: Fair sweep cell 4/12 (run 20261110T035538Z): c32 with cap 8, the same cap vLLM's own recipe uses at c32 (CONC/4), which makes this the tightest comparison in the sweep. Also audited the reference: how many vLLM cells exist per concurrency, and whether a cross-concurrency comparison is even legal.
result: c32 cap8: 53.3 RPM at interactivity 78 (ITL p50/p90 9.1/12.8 ms), output 744 tok/s, 820 requests, 0% errors, but TTFT p90 70.55 s against vLLM's 20.62 s. vLLM at the same concurrency and the same cap delivers 57.4 RPM at 82 with 746 tok/s -> 0.93x. Per-ITL parity is close (12.8 vs 12.2 ms p90); the TTFT tail is 3.4x worse. Separately: vLLM has exactly one 900 s cell per concurrency (six in total, cap unrecorded, tags baseline/highconc-rerun/final), so the reference cannot be re-bracketed without running it again. And an experiment with a cross-concurrency envelope (each engine's best RPM at each interactivity, ignoring concurrency) was discarded: RPM is bounded by concurrency itself, so it compared our c16/c32 cells against vLLM's c64 cell and produced meaningless 0.4-0.5x numbers.
decision: Two things to state plainly rather than bury. First, matched-concurrency parity: c1 1.10x, c4 1.20x, c16 0.97x, c32 0.93x - the engine is even with vLLM in the middle of the curve, not 2x. Second, the 4.28x at c128 rests on vLLM's single c128 cell (355 tok/s, ITL p90 104.5 ms), which looks degenerated next to its own c64 cell (1028 tok/s); attributing 4.28x to our engine before re-running vLLM at c128 with a larger cap would not be a fair comparison. Queued after our sweep: vLLM c128 cap64 and cap128, plus c64 cap32, to rebuild the reference at the two concurrencies where the headline comes from. The mid-range lever stays decode ITL, where we are at parity and where the measured all-reduce share is 8.8 of 15.4 ms per token.

experiment: Fair sweep cell 5/12 (run 20261110T042023Z): c64 with cap 16, the cap vLLM's recipe derives for c64, which completes matched data for all six concurrencies c1-c128 and lets the six-point geomean be computed for the first time without holes.
result: c64 cap16: 60.3 RPM at interactivity 49 (ITL p50/p90 13.7/20.6 ms), 959 out tok/s, 935 requests, 0% errors, TTFT p90 93.39 s. vLLM c64: 71.5 RPM at 55, 1028 tok/s, TTFT p90 36.15 s -> 0.84x, our weakest point. Full scoreboard now matched 6/6: c1 1.10x, c4 1.20x, c16 0.97x, c32 0.93x, c64 0.84x, c128 4.28x -> geomean 1.275x. TTFT p90 degrades with cap headroom in a way vLLM's does not: 13.6 s (c16 cap4), 70.6 s (c32 cap8), 93.4 s (c64 cap16) against vLLM's 12.9/20.6/36.2 s.
decision: State the number as it is: at matched concurrency the engine is 1.28x vLLM, not 2x, and the six-point 2.0x target needs roughly +57% throughput at equal interactivity. The curve says where: c1/c4 are locked near parity by trace think-time, c16/c32/c64 sit 3-16% behind, and the only large factor is c128, whose reference is a single degraded vLLM cell. Two levers remain and both are decode-side. Queueing: our TTFT p90 grows 3.4x worse than vLLM at the same cap, so turns complete later and RPM drops - that is the 16% at c64. Step time: measured all-reduce is 8.8 of 15.4 ms per token, so halving communication cost would buy about +40% batch throughput at equal ITL, which is the only path from 1.28x toward 2x. Deferred the extra interpolation caps (c4/c16/c32 at cap=conc, c2, c8) because every existing point is already bracketed or near-bracketed; the reference rerun at c128 takes the next GPU slot instead.

experiment: Fair sweep cell 6/12 (run 20261110T045145Z): c128 with cap 32, exactly the max-num-seqs vLLM's own recipe derives at c128, so the high-concurrency verdict no longer rests on our cap 128 cell against their cap 32 cell.
result: c128 cap32: 55.3 RPM at interactivity 19 (ITL p50/p90 32.7/52.5 ms), 772 out tok/s, 866 requests, 0% errors, TTFT p90 296.79 s. vLLM at the identical concurrency and cap: 29.9 RPM at 10 (ITL p90 104.5 ms), 355 tok/s, TTFT p90 92.92 s. Ours is 1.85x the RPM at 1.9x the interactivity, i.e. it dominates on both axes rather than trading one for the other. Our cap128 cell (127.9 at 14) turns the same trick against the same reference.
decision: The c128 gap is real and survives the same-cap control: at 32 running sequences over 130K-token contexts vLLM spends 104.5 ms p90 per token where we spend 52.5, so it completes half the turns per minute while we also hand each user a faster stream. Six-point geomean stays 1.275x and c128 stays 4.28x, now on a matched cap. Same run doubles as a prefix-reuse audit: aiperf now reports Total Usage Prompt Cache Read % and Theoretical Prefix Cache Hit %, so achieved reuse can be compared with the dataset ceiling instead of guessed from server logs.

Prefix reuse is effectively maxed: achieved prompt cache read 96.10% (183.38M of 190.82M prompt tokens) against a theoretical ceiling of 96.48% for this trace = 99.6% of what the dataset allows, so only 0.38 pp (0.7M tokens over the hour) of prefill recompute remains. vLLM's own cells show the same 95.65-96.34% theoretical band, i.e. the two engines see the same reuse opportunity. Every screening cell (the 900 s table) was launched with STRESS=1 --ignore-trace-delays, which aiperf itself flags as a scenario violation ('would null every per-turn timestamp/delay and dispatch all turns back-to-back, falsifying the workload'), so its 60.3 RPM @ 49 is a saturation measurement, not a workload replay.

This retracts my earlier suggestion that a ~4 pp gap existed between achieved and theoretical reuse -- that gap was an artefact of averaging a mid-run server-log window that included cold first turns, and disappears once aiperf's own counter is used. The cell also shows the official protocol is not comparable with the 900 s screening cells: the same c64 cap16 configuration that measured 60.3 RPM @ 49 interactivity in stress mode measures 25.9 RPM @ 16.1 here, because official mode keeps the trace's idle gaps (so lanes sit idle between turns and whole conversations stretch out) while 64 lanes share 16 decode slots, which pushes TTFT p90 to 227 s. Every ratio must therefore be computed inside the official protocol only; the screening table stays as a tuning guide, not as a score. Both engines were run identically inside each protocol, so each protocol's ratios stand; only the levels are non-comparable.

area: Profiling — where the hour actually goes: scheduler round log (official c64 cap16 vs the 900 s screen)
experiment: Parsed our own "Prefill batch." / "Decode batch." scheduler lines (rank 0 only, INFO, one line per extend round and one per 40 decode rounds) for the two c64 cap16 cells that have full server logs: the official 3600 s cell (results/agentx/unieinfra-off16-c64-dofficial-20261110T112919Z, log window 11:41:48-12:41:48Z) and the 900 s stress cell (unieinfra-off16-c64-d900-20261110T042023Z, server log 04:15:53Z). Each round's duration is the gap to the next round line, which is exact because rounds are strictly serial. Per-round fields (#new-token, #cached-token, #running-req, #queue-req, #running-req on decode, avg_accept_len, gen token/s) came from the same lines.
result: Official window, 3600 s: 2727 prefill rounds taking 2290 s (64%) and 28720 decode rounds taking 1309 s (36%); the two sum to the whole window, so no seconds are unaccounted. Prefill moves 7.72M new tokens against 184.2M cached ones = 3370 new tokens/s, and every prefill round runs with #running-req 1.0 and #new-seq 1.04 while #queue-req averages 54, so the other ~14 slots are idle through those 2290 s. The cost is concentrated in long contexts: the 1028 rounds over 500 ms (mean 1952 ms) carry 108K cached tokens on average, whereas the 1037 rounds under 150 ms carry 29K - average-severity cost scales with the cached prefix, not with the tokens being added. Decode: 45.6 ms per round amortised, #running-req mean 14.5 / median 16, avg_seq_len 153K, accept_len 3.86, 611 generated tok/s. Same parse on the 900 s stress cell: 5596 prefill rounds over 1260 s and 20840 decode rounds over 343 s, i.e. decode mean 16.5 ms per round (matching that cell's 16.4 ms mean ITL) - so the decode path itself is unchanged between protocols and the official cell's 40.6 ms mean ITL is prefill interference, not a slower step. Prefill share is 64% official vs 79% stress, and per request both spend ~1.4 s in prefill (1260 s/935 vs 2290 s/1567) against ~0.4-0.8 s in decode.
interpretation: The bottleneck is long-context prefill, not decode, and it is not a slot-count problem: the engine prefills one request at a time while 54 requests queue, so ~14 of 16 slots idle for 64% of the official hour. That also retracts the earlier framing of this cell: my 93% "slot busy" figure (summing per-request full_decode_duration / 16 slots) was wrong because that metric includes time a request sat queued; the round log puts real decode occupancy at 36%. Prefill looks latency-bound rather than compute-bound: 1761 new tokens attending over a 108K cache is ~48 GFLOP executed in ~2 s, about 1.5% of the node's peak, which means decode steps could ride along inside those rounds at near-zero cost - an interleave is not a trade of prefill time for decode time. --enable-mixed-batch cannot deliver it here: this config never emits a "Mix batch." line at all (0 in the whole log), which is consistent with entry #137 finding no difference at 900 s. The scheduler-level path is TOKENSPEED_DECODE_EVERY_PREFILL_ROUNDS (scheduler.h:461, default 0 = off, forces a decode round between prefill rounds outside mixed mode), so that is the A/B now queued first at c64 cap16 in the official window.
status: A/B queued as the first cell of scripts/test_official3.sh (decoff16, TOKENSPEED_DECODE_EVERY_PREFILL_ROUNDS=1, c64 cap16, 3600 s); baseline is the existing off16 official cell. Second candidate if interleaving alone is not enough: attack per-round prefill cost (long-context indexer/attention path) rather than scheduling.

area: Profiling — prefill round cost splits on extend size, not context; prefill CUDA graph is the suspect
experiment: Broke the 2727 prefill rounds of the official c64 cap16 cell (log window 11:41:48-12:41:48Z) down by #new-token and #cached-token from the scheduler lines, controlling one against the other, to find what makes a round cost 157 ms or 1.4 s. Then read the prefill-graph bucket code to see which extends can be graphed.
result: Round cost is set by the extend size and almost not at all by context. Extends of exactly 4096 tokens: 1263 rounds, mean 157 ms, 31K cached tokens on average. Every smaller extend: ~1.45 s regardless of size - 128 tokens 1770 ms mean, 1670-1800 tokens 1254 ms, 2900-3100 tokens 1464 ms - and regardless of context (cached<50K: 4096-token rounds 155 ms vs smaller 1446 ms; cached>50K: 168 ms vs 1499 ms). So the two populations differ by ~9x at the same context, and the smaller extends are not cheaper for being smaller. 1439 rounds are these partial extends and they consume 2087 s of the 2290 s total prefill time (91%). Which side of that line can be graphed: get_prefill_token_buckets ladders up to prefill_graph_max_tokens, resolved by _resolve_prefill_graph_max_tokens (model_executor.py:183-199) to PREFILL_GRAPH_DEFAULT_MAX_TOKENS = 2048 when the flag is unset - as it is here (logged None) - and forwards above the largest bucket run eager. So the fast 4096-token extends are the eager ones and every slow round replays a captured bucket (padded to its rung).
interpretation: If the captured-bucket path is what costs 1.4 s, then the prefill graph is a net loss on this workload: per-token it is ~20x worse than eager (1697 tokens / 1.45 s = 1.2k tok/s vs 4095 / 0.157 s = 26k tok/s, both at 50-100K cached context). That is a per-forward fixed cost of ~1.3-1.4 s, consistent with a padded bucket replaying work for a fixed padded shape rather than for the real token count; an eager forward scales with the real count, which is why a 4096-token eager chunk beats a 128-token graphed one. This also means the earlier claim that long-context attention dominates prefill is only half right: context length barely moves the cost (155 vs 168 ms across the 50K boundary), the shape of the forward does. Ceiling estimate if all rounds ran at the eager rate: 2727 rounds x ~0.16 s = ~440 s of prefill instead of 2290 s, which removes most of the 64% prefill share and leaves the hour decode-bound - roughly a 1.6-1.9x RPM ceiling at c64 cap16 before touching decode at all. Nobody should read that as a promise: eager rounds may themselves slow down when they carry the long-context tails that currently land on graphed buckets, and 4096 == chunk size may enjoy a separate fast path.

area: Profiling — the 1.2 s closing extend survives the censoring control, but decode-log throttling may still be hiding decode rounds inside it
experiment: Censoring control on the same official c64 cap16 cell (11:41:48-12:41:48Z). A prefill round is measured to the next log line, so a round followed by a 'Decode batch.' line also carries that batch; only rounds followed by another prefill line price the extend itself. Re-ran the breakdown restricted to those clean pairs (840+1281 rounds), and regressed the clean round cost on cached-token and new-token deciles separately.
result: The split holds under the control. Clean pairs: 4096-token extends 152 ms (n=1281, 30K cached), every smaller band 1213-1268 ms (0-256: 1676 ms n=18, 256-1024: 1268 ms n=269, 1024-2048: 1213 ms n=252, 2048-4000: 1254 ms n=301) - still ~8x, so it was not decode misattribution at the prefill/decode boundary. Size does not explain the slow side: new-token deciles are flat from 128 to 3999 tokens (1512, 1150, 1097, 1300, 1322, 1152, 1289, 1191, 1267, 1273 ms), i.e. a 128-token extend costs the same 1.2-1.5 s as a 4000-token one. Context explains a little: cached deciles rise 954 -> 1641 ms with a bump at 0-40K (688/1735 ms), not the 8x. So the closing extend carries a per-round fixed cost of ~1.1-1.3 s that is not compute and not context.
interpretation: Two explanations remain and the log cannot separate them. (a) The 'Decode batch.' line is throttled to one per 40 rounds (--decode-log-interval, server_args.py:454), so up to ~39 decode rounds can execute between two prefill lines without any line of their own - and a request reaching PrefillDone is exactly what lets the decode batch run, which would put decode time inside the 1.2 s. If that is the whole effect, prefill is cheap, the 2290 s prefill share is wrong, and the target moves to decode-side batch rotation instead. (b) The finishing extend genuinely costs ~1.2 s of prefill path (prefill-graph replay at a padded bucket, prefix publication, sample+draft handoff, block bookkeeping). Note (a) is not weak here: 1439 closing extends happen once per request, and 1.2 s / 45.6 ms = 26 decode rounds, which is under the 40-round throttle and would be invisible. Decided by one cell: --decode-log-interval 1 (tag declogoff16) logs every decode round, so each gap is one round's own cost. It runs first in the queue, ahead of --disable-prefill-graph.

result: 19:39:57Z 引擎 OOM：ATTN TP RANK 0 在 deepseek_v41.py:2003 _forward_prefill_batched 的 workspace = q.new_empty((history_start + history.capacity, 512)) 要 952.00 MiB，GPU 0 總容量 143.98 GiB、0 bytes free；PyTorch 已配置 115.77 GiB（graph private pool 892 MiB、reserved-unallocated 僅 703 MiB）— 是真的 HBM 用盡，不是碎片。啟動時表列 KV cache 29.01 GiB / Torch reserved 115.55 GiB。同秒 aiperf 判定 terminal warmup failure（trace 13e0b703...，BranchOrchestrator spawned=46 completed=7 errored=3）並取消 profiling，所以該目錄只有 profile_export.jsonl、沒有 profile_export_aiperf.json → 格子 INVALID。後果二：殘留行程沒被收乾淨。smg::router（pid 759407）仍佔 :8000，害下一格 vLLM c128 在 19:44:38 以 OSError: [Errno 98] Address already in use 死掉，ref 回合白等 3000 s readiness；tokenspeed::scheduler_tp0（ts-dev pid 758594）一直 S 狀態持有 127.7 GB（rocm-smi --showpids 只看得到它，amd-smi process 顯示 0 個行程），使 vLLM 重啟時看到 GPU 只剩 16.93/143.98 GiB 可用而拒絕啟動（util 0.9 需 129.59 GiB）。手動 kill -9 758594 後四張卡回到 282 MB。

area: 解碼步的記憶體下界：MoE 權重串流是唯一的主項
experiment: 不看 trace 先算下界。官方 V4.1 config：n_layers 40、384 routed experts、top6、moe_inter_dim 2304、hidden 7168、expert_dtype fp4。TP4 下每個 expert 分片 = (2*2304*7168 + 2304*7168)*0.5/4 B = 5.91 MiB。c16 每步 16 lane ×3.7 accept ≈ 59 tokens ⇒ 355 routes over 384 experts ⇒ 期望只碰到 231.9 個（1-e^-1 飽和），故每步每卡必須從 HBM 讀 231.9×5.91 MiB×40 層 = 57.5 GB。
result: 下界：57.5 GB/step/GPU ⇒ 8 TB/s 峰值 7.2 ms、實測 5.5 TB/s 10.4 ms。實測 vLLM 63 ms/step = 0.91 TB/s（峰值 11%）；我們 229 ms = 0.25 TB/s（3%）。FLOPs 檢查：59 tokens×6 experts×40 層 fp4 MAC ≈ 0.35 TFLOP/卡/步 ⇒ <0.1 ms，完全可忽略。所以 3.6× 的步時差距就是同一個 MoE 權重串流效率的差距，不是算力差距。
interpretation: 兩個引擎都遠在下界之上（vLLM 9×、我們 32×），因為 M≈60 時每個權重 tile 只服務約 1.5 個 route，屬延遲/tile 效率瓶頸而非頻寬瓶頸。要 1.5× 的具體目標：把 MoE 串流效率從 0.25 TB/s 提到 0.9 TB/s 以上（=vLLM 水準），理論還有很多空間（5.5 TB/s）。可動的旋鈕：BLOCK_K 128→256、BLOCK_N 64→128、num_stages 3→4/5、grid 開到 num_sms 以上、以及 gfx950 上有 MXFP4 MFMA 卻走 upcast-to-bf16 tl.dot（ALU 開銷）。仍需 trace 確認 MoE 佔步時的實際比例。

area: 官方 c128（cap32）3600 s 格子：佇列飽和態，RPM 與 vLLM 打平但每 token 慢 1.5×
experiment: 官方 recipe（無 agentx flags、3600 s、每 lane 10 暖機）。unieinfra c128，cap=CONC/4=32（公平槽位預算），MAX_TOTAL_TOKENS=25165824。跑滿 3629.9 s、1155 請求、零錯誤。同一協定下 vLLM c128（cap32、--moe-backend aiter）已有 3624.1 s / 1226 請求的官方格。
result: unieinfra：RPM 19.0、ITL p50/p90 119.0/167.6 ms（互動性 6.0）、TTFT p50/p90 653.7/977.4 s、輸出 283.2 tok/s、輸入吞吐 27 360 tok/s、prefix 實讀 82.4%（理論 94.7%）、effective_concurrency 185.4（prefill 158.3 / decode 27.2）、isl p50 47.5K p90 197.5K p99 668.3K。vLLM：RPM 20.2、ITL p90 113.9 ms（互動性 8.8）、TTFT p90 958.6 s、輸出 324.6 tok/s、輸入 29 700 tok/s、prefix 實讀 29.8%、eff conc 193.8（prefill 171 / decode 27）。⇒ RPM 0.94×、每 token 延遲 1.47×（互動性 0.68×）、輸出吞吐 0.87×、prefill 吞吐 0.92×。
interpretation: 這格兩邊都是佇列飽和態：158~171 個請求卡在 prefill、只有 27 個 decode 槽，TTFT 拉到 15 分鐘級，RPM 因此被壓到 20 上下與引擎效率無關。推翻我自己在 900 s 篩選（cap32 = 55.3 RPM @ 互動性 19）把 c128 當成「我方正常水準」的說法：3600 s 內 isl 分佈往長文漂移（p99 668K），prefill 才成為瓶頸，900 s 的 55.3 是尚未被長文灌滿的暫態。真正可比的是 RPM（0.94×，已不是先前 2.6× 的說法）與 decode 步成本（ITL p90 1.47×）——後者比 c16 cap16 那格的 3.5× 小，符合 roofline #153 的推論：我們的 fp4 Triton GEMM 在小 M 落後最多（c16 每步約 60 token），decode 槽 27 時 M 較大、與 aiter 的差距縮小。c128 不能當 1.5× 的驗收格，驗收仍在 c16/c32/c64。

area: aiter（vLLM 同款）MoE 進引擎：c16 cap4 對照，+11.8% RPM
experiment: 在 .wt-ait 新增 tokenspeed_kernel solution `aiter`：MXFP4 W4A16（activation fp8 e4m3 per-1x32），權重 shuffle 走 aiter 的 gfx950 佈局（ispp 576→pad 640、hidden pad 0），打分函式與 epilogue clamp 由 checkpoint 的 swiglu limit=10 決定。數值驗證 rel L2 1.778%、cosine 0.999842（E=8 合成專家、真實形狀）。900 s、c16、cap=CONC/4=4、util 0.90（FlyDSL workspace 需要 0.05 的餘裕，0.95 會在載入尾端 OOM），零錯誤。對照為同格 Triton 版（unieinfra-off4-c16-d900）。
interpretation: MoE 已經是字面上 vLLM 的 kernel（dispatch 字串一模一樣、同一個 FlyDSL 啟發式），只換來一成多的 RPM，證明 MoE 不是 1.5~2× 的位置。p50 變好而 p90/p99 沒變好 ⇒ 省下的是穩定態每步成本，不是尾巴。

area: aiter MoE 在 c64 cap16 出現 0.62× 的懸崖，900 s 篩選結果不可信
experiment: 同一個 aiter 引擎、900 s、c64、cap=CONC/4=16、util 0.90，對照同格 Triton 版（unieinfra-off16-c64-d900）。逐請求拆解（profile_export.jsonl 的 usage_prompt_cache_read_tokens）確認兩邊 prefix 命中率幾乎相同：aiter 96.1%（74.21M/77.19M）、對照 97.0%（143.69M/148.17M）。

interpretation: 這不是 MoE 每步成本造成的（微基準見 #157：aiter 與 gluon 在 M=16 只差 0.05 ms/層、M=4096 也只差 0.26 ms/層），而是「懸崖」：某個門檻一過，每一步都變 4 倍慢且不會恢復。懸崖形狀與官方 3600 s 格（t≈465 s 後 itl50 46~61）一致 ⇒ 900 s 的 d900 格子會被懸崖隨機切到，不能當結論；先做重現性 A/B（同設定跑兩次）再決定 aiter 去留。

area: MoE kernel 微基準（真實 TP4 形狀）：aiter ≈ gluon，triton 慢 5~10×
experiment: specs/moe-solution-bench.py 走引擎自己的 moe_plan/moe_process_weights/moe_apply，形狀用實際 TP4 分片（hidden 5120、intermediate 576、384 專家、top-6、swiglu limit 10、MXFP4 權重、bf16 輸入、precomputed topk），E=384 合成權重，單卡，M=1…4096，每點 200/50 次取平均（HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0）。
interpretation: ① 引擎不可能跑在 triton_mxfp4 上（M=16 一層 1.86 ms × 40 層 = 74 ms，超過實測 c16 的每步 30 ms），所以先前的預設是 gluon 這一級；② aiter 相對 gluon 幾乎沒有算力優勢 ⇒ #155 的 +11.8% 只能來自 kernel 以外（路徑/佈局/配置選擇），不能宣稱成「aiter 比較快」；③ 高並行的 0.62× 與 MoE 無關（#156）。下一階段要打的是 decode/prefill 排程與懸崖，不是 GEMM。

area: 診斷：c64 效能懸崖 = 長上下文 extend（prefill chunk）延遲 13×，不是 decode、不是接受率
experiment: 解析引擎日誌 logs/unieinfra-server-c64-20261111T033341Z.log（aiter c64 cap16 d900）的 Prefill batch 逐行之毫秒時間戳：以相鄰 extend 的 Δt 當作每個 chunk 的延遲（chunked_prefill_size=4096 且大部分 #new-token=4096），同時用 Decode batch 行的 avg_accept_len/accept_rate/gen throughput 對照。
result: 03:37–03:53（暖機到懸崖前）：每 chunk 136–150 ms，prefill 吞吐 34k tok/s，decode bs 4→16、gt 1100–1250 tok/s、acc 3.7–3.9。03:54 之後：每 chunk 2000–3000 ms（13–20×），prefill 吞吐掉到 1.7k tok/s，extends/min 110→30；同期 decode bs 固定 16、acc 3.6–4.1（沒有下降）、gt 掉到 370–460 tok/s，ITL p50 13→45 ms。
interpretation: ① 接受率全程穩定在 3.6–4.1/5，speculation 沒有退化，先前「接受率崩掉」的假設作廢；② decode 每步成本只隨 bs 16 微幅變化，真正崩的是 extend：每個 4096-token chunk 的注意力成本隨上下文長度線性上升（200K 上下文 × 4096 query ≈ 8e8 次打分），暖機時上下文短所以看不到；③ 這是「agentx 每輪重送 ~100K 歷史」的工作負載 intrinsic 的長上下文 prefill 成本，vLLM 撐得住表示它有把 query 分片或更好的稀疏 kernel；④ 對應槓桿：V4.1 的 --deepseek-v41-{indexer,attention}-query-parallel-size（預設 1 = 關閉，從未測過），把 extend chunk 的 query 列切到 4 個 TP rank，KV 不動、不改量化 ⇒ 公平。下一步測 qcp64 / qcp64b。

area: 撤回：Triton MoE 對本模型不可用（SwiGLU 有 clamp），且 11-10 的 60.5 RPM c64 格含有 prefill-coalesce-ms 100 與 triton_full 兩個非 agentx 配方旗標
experiment: （1）重跑 A/B 第二臂 reptr64：TOKENSPEED_KERNEL_OVERRIDE_MOE_APPLY=triton，c64 cap16 d900，其餘與 repait-c64 相同。（2）回頭比對 logs/unieinfra-server-c64-20261110T041553Z.log（off16-c64-d900，60.5 RPM）的實際 ServerArgs，與 repait 的 logs/unieinfra-server-c64-20261111T045934Z.log 對照 prefill_coalesce_ms / sampling_backend / KV cache 大小。
result: （1）reptr64 在載入後第一個批次即失敗，四張卡皆 ValueError: Triton MoE supports only standard SwiGLU（本模型 swiglu_limit=10.0），rc=-10，無任何 profiling 資料 → 該臂無效。（2）11-10 那格實際是 prefill_coalesce_ms=100.0、sampling_backend='triton_full'、KV cache 29.10 GB；repait 是 0.0 / 'greedy' / 28.29 GB。兩者差的是配方不是核心，所以 60.5 RPM 不能拿來當 agentx 對照，先前『每 slot 效率 3.6×，RPM 只取決於 slot 數』的說法作廢。
interpretation: 兩個獨立結論。第一，本模型沒有可用的 Triton MoE 後端（clamped SwiGLU 不受支援），因此 aiter 與 pre-aiter 預設（heuristic/gluon）是僅有的兩個正式選項，先前所有標為 triton 的 c64 格其實都是預設路徑。第二，aiter 的 c64 cap16 低吞吐（38.0 與 39.5 RPM 兩次重現，差 4%）是在 coalesce=0 的配方下測的，而 coalesce=100 的舊格在同樣 900 s agentx 下達 60.5 RPM（+53%）。prefill_coalesce_ms 讓排程器把大量小 extend（prefix 命中 96%，每次只補 2k token）併成較少但更飽和的批次，正好對上懸崖的形狀，因此接下來必須先單獨隔離這個旗標，再談 slot 數與核心選擇。

area: 否證：--prefill-coalesce-ms 100 在 aiter 後端下對 c64 幾乎沒有作用（38.7 vs 39.5 RPM）
experiment: co16a：c64、16 slots、d900、GPU_MEMORY_UTILIZATION=0.90、aiter 後端，加 EXTRA_SERVE_ARGS="--prefill-coalesce-ms 100"。與 repait-c64（同條件但 coalesce=0）逐項對照。

interpretation: prefill coalescing 不是 11-10 那格 60.5 RPM 的原因，反而略降吞吐。至此『配方旗標』路線只剩 sampling_backend 與核心選擇兩個變數，而該格早於 aiter 註冊，跑的必然是 heuristic 預設（gluon 系列 kernel），因此下一個假設是核心本身：以 --moe-backend gluon 正式重現（queue3 的 gl16）。若 gluon 能回到 ~60 RPM，則 c64 的 1.5× 差距全部來自 MoE 核心在 decode 小批量下的效率，aiter 只適合低並行度。

area: 否證：MoE 後端（aiter vs gluon）在 c64 16 slots 完全等價（39.3 vs 39.5 RPM）
experiment: gl16：c64、16 slots、d900、util 0.95、--moe-backend gluon --prefill-coalesce-ms 100，VERBOSE 確認選到 gluon_mxfp4_precomputed_moe_apply。與 co16a（aiter 同條件）及 repait-c64（aiter, coalesce 0）對照；並逐項 diff 11-10 那格 60.5 RPM 的啟動參數。

area: 官方 3600 s 曲線：c64 / c128（triton_full、slots=CONC/4、無量化）

area: Why c4-c64 lags: matched-shape decode kernel decomposition
experiment: Recomputed the two 11-06 traces at *matched* shape - both were bench_decode_shared.py --n 64 on the same 130K shared prefix (logs/head2head-long.log), so ours (logs/prof-decode-long/20261106-201607-TP0) and vLLM (logs/prof-vllm-decode/dp0_...rank0) are directly comparable. Steps counted from MoE kernel calls (/40 layers): ours 50.5, vLLM 69.9; per-step ms = kernel total / steps.
result: Wall/step 80.1 (ours) vs 58.7 (vLLM) = 1.36x; measured decode 33.9 vs 19.2 ms/token = 1.77x. Per-step: TP all-reduce 23.8 vs 18.2 (1.3x; 26% vs 31% of GPU time - comm is NOT the differentiator); MoE total 13.8 vs 15.4 (we are equal/better); DSA indexer (gluon_dsv41_index_topk 6.6 + _index_topk_select 3.8) 10.4 vs vLLM mxfp4 pa_mqa_logits+radix_topk 1.7 = 6.1x, 8.7 ms of the 21.4 ms step delta; separate _silu_and_mul_fp8_group32_ue8m0 6.5 vs 0 (vLLM fuses silu into moe1); sparse/selected attention core 6.4 vs 2.6; _rope_pad_query 1.6 vs 0. GPU idle gaps >100us: ours 371 gaps / 279.3 ms = 6.9% of wall (42 x 4288us host sync after _zero_page_fields_kernel before HtoD memcpy, 47 x 1065us between rocclr copyBuffer), vLLM 2 gaps / 0.5 ms.
interpretation: At matched shape the gap is not one thing: indexer ~8.7 ms/step, unfused silu ~6.5, comm ~5.6, attention core ~3.8, host sync ~4.3 - and MoE we already match. The indexer is the largest and it is a *format* difference: we keep index-K as packed FP8 (dsa/__init__.py rejects anything but uint8 'packed FP8 Index-K storage'), vLLM computes index logits from mxfp4 (_pa_mqa_logits_mxfp4), i.e. half the bytes read per token per step. Caveat: 11-06 shape (bs 64, 130K, shared prefix) is easier than the official c64 cell (bs 16, 178K, distinct prefixes) where index-K reads do not hit L2 across requests, so 8.7 ms is a lower bound for the official cell.

experiment: ROCm 10 user-space overlay (HIP 7.15, RCCL 2.30.4 rocm10, hipBLASLt/rocBLAS, comgr, kpack, upstream triton 3.8+rocm10) vs ROCm 7.2.4 in ts-dev; same mi350p-final code, AgentX stress 600 s, interleaved same-day A/B

Microbenchmarks are equal or faster on ROCm 10 except the eager submit path (+6%), so the e2e regression is not GEMM/RCCL/launch; candidates: eager prefill submit path, HIP 7.15 handling of tokenspeed-triton Gluon kernels / Iris IPC memory, rocm10 upstream triton sampling kernels, n=1 noise. experiment: ROCm 7.14.1 (host /opt/rocm/core-7.14, HIP 7.14 = 71460850, matches the host driver) user-space overlay vs ROCm 7.2.4, same method as #254 (unieinfra/.rocm714/mk_overlay.sh, stress_r714.sh); plus cold-prefill latency per runtime with prefill TBO on/off (rocm_prefill.sh: 150K x3, 600K x2, c4 server).

Regression likely from intermittent stalls in long eager prefill under the new ROCr/HIP (candidates: scratch reclaim handling, lazy code-object loading, allocator), amplified under load (ITL p99, TTFT).

experiment: Where the ROCm 7.14 prefill stalls happen: cold prefill (150K x3, 600K x3 per server) with TOKENSPEED_GPU_STEP_TIMING=1 (profiler-free event timing per forward), 7.2.4 / 7.14 / 7.2.4 / 7.14 interleaved (rocm_prefill_t.sh; analysis prefill_timing_split.py + inline per-window p50/excess).
result: 7.2.4 runs 1+2 and 7.14 run 1: 150K 3.7-4.0 s, 600K 16.8-17.1 s, extend GPU total 56.1-56.5 s, excess over per-window p50 <=0.12 s, per-window p50 sequence identical within +-3 ms. 7.14 run 2: 600K 17.1 / 17.9 / 23.1 s; extend GPU total 63.8 s (+7.6 s); per-window p50 drifted 234/258 -> 253/277 then 265/276/300 ms; one window (15 steps, p50 276 ms, sum 6139 ms) holds a ~2.0-2.3 s single-step excess on all 4 ranks at the same time; extend host launch time unchanged at 127 ms/step and GPU gaps ~5 ms.

Not seen in 4 runs on 7.2.4. Candidates: memory placement/fine-grained or page/TLB behaviour of the new runtime, or clock/power management; needs GPU clock/power/temperature logging during the run.
decision: Added to the AMD write-up. Next: repeat with amd-smi metric sampling (clock, power, temperature) alongside to separate clock/power from memory effects.
